reasoning_traces.think:
The hybrid uncertainty score U_{i,t} aggregates multiple uncertainty signals—diversity D, contradiction C, sampling agreement S, retrieval relevance R, entropy H, and calibration gap G—into a scalar measure of forecast reliability. This is modeled using a sigmoid function of linear combinations of these components, weighted by validation-fitted coefficients. The controller then applies a threshold θ to decide whether to issue a forecast or abstain. This framework enables selective forecasting by dynamically adjusting confidence thresholds based on observed uncertainty. Dualities emerge in how uncertainty manifests: e.g., low diversity (D) implies over-reliance on one source, while high entropy (H) indicates ambiguous outcomes. Failure modes include overfitting to validation data, poor calibration of individual components, or misalignment between agent outputs and the hybrid score. In GSE, this translates to a dynamic risk-weighted belief update where high-U predictions trigger fallback behaviors like manual review or reduced exposure.
